title: SKIP TUTORIAL is built: a button in the opening and ?skip=defence, opening a real run at the back door with the Relay and the Mortar earned
context: The accepted entry 2026-09-16-skip-tutorial-into-the-back-door left three things open: whether the skip is a bookmarkable URL or only a button, whether the campaign's own sector 1 is skipped outright, and how Isao explains the situation in two lines. The owner asked while playtesting with friends in mind, so the entry point had to be player-facing and shareable, not another developer jump carrying acceptance hooks.
outcome: All three are answered and shipped. (1) BOTH: `index.html?skip=defence#td` is the URL a friend can bookmark and `src/fx/skip-tutorial.js` is the button. `skipsTutorial` in src/core/story-route.js makes ?skip= name the story the way ?story= does, so the link needs no acceptance switch and never lands on the campaign board; `skipTutorialUrl` builds the button's href by dropping the opening's keys (stage, story, grow, phase, threat) and keeping the rest, so a click inside a harness run stays a harness run. The button is bottom-right in the story's monochrome (styles.css #skip-tutorial), created only in the story world and only when this run is not itself the skip, and it removes itself the moment the run is automated -- the handover dismisses it if the player does not. It is mirrored as the wired SKIP TUTORIAL entry in STORY_JUMPS (src/content/nav.js), pointing at the same player URL. (2) SECTOR 1 IS SKIPPED OUTRIGHT: createSectorRun takes a `firstSector` hook and the skipped run opens at sector 2, THE BACK DOOR, so the collapse behind the bays, its breach, SOL-82 coming online and the array's refill all arrive through the sector table rather than through a special case. (3) Isao's two lines are the new `skip_defence` brief in src/isaobriefs.js -- 'Base is printed, Relay and Mortar are ours, SOL-82 answers when we call.' / 'The rock behind the bays is about to give. Build, and hold the back door.' -- shown on arrival. The rest of the starting state: STORY_SKIP in src/content/story-defaults.js pins stage 8 (the base standing through the bays, so the three hulls read as lives), phase 'expedition' (towers automatic), 450 kg of biomass and the two parts; readStoryQuery applies them and forces grow off and the full threat of a real run, not a deep link's sparse 0.35; a new pure rule `deliverAtOnce` and a glue method `preDeliver` put the Relay and the Mortar home as though rocket-a and rocket-b had come back, raising each site's flag with no crate beside it (cargo.raiseFlag now takes { crate, standing }) and standing two trophies in the row at the landing; the shield rack is filled and the array refilled. It is a real run: waves come on the run's own clock, the gate can break, the debrief follows and CONTINUE moves to sector 3. No acceptance-only hook is switched on -- ?skip=defence carries no acceptance=1, and the harness adds its own. A bare index.html still plays the tutorial from the landing, now with the offer on it.
alternatives: A button that mutates the running game into the skipped state instead of navigating; rejected, a browser document owns one game lifetime (docs/STATE.md, Boundaries) and every route change already reloads -- a link is the cheap and honest form.

Leaving the site flags down at the two pre-delivered sites, which is what the real delivery flow does (glue.step lowers the flag when the part comes home); rejected on the owner's wording, and the crate is suppressed instead so the site does not read as still holding its part.
Reusing the DEFENSE developer jump URL for friends; rejected as before -- acceptance hooks, no towers, no threat.
Starting the skipped run at sector 1 and letting the back door arrive a sector later; rejected, the ask is the back-door fight as the first thing seen.
evidence: npm test (120 test programs) and npm run check green on every commit; new cases in test/story-route.mjs (the skip URL is the story, both spellings, the href rewrite), test/expeditions.mjs (deliverAtOnce gives relay and mortar and reveals nothing else) and test/nav-content.mjs (the drawer's jump is the player URL).

scripts/browser-test.mjs --skip-tutorial: the opening still plays the tutorial and carries the offer; a real pointer click on #skip-tutorial lands on ?skip=defence; the run there is automated at phase expedition with unlocked = rotor, quiver, relay, mortar, two flags up and two trophies home, three hulls, three bays, 620 kg, a full rack, a charged array; the build menu offers the Relay and the Mortar and still reads PART OUT on the lancer and the plasma; sector 2 THE BACK DOOR opens with one breach behind the bays and one on the gate side, SOL-82 online, and a wave arrives without being asked (15 enemies, A/gate 1/4, B/back 1/4).
The same run fought to the end: SECTOR SECURE at 33 s with both breaches HELD, the debrief card, and CONTINUE into sector 3.

Screenshots artifacts/browser/skip-tutorial-offer.png, -arrival.png, -back-door-fight.png. The first fight screenshot was a picture of bare lattice because the step's own build-menu probe opens the radial on the first placeable cell on the planet and takes the build camera there; the probe now runs after the fight is photographed.
src/td-tab.js stays at its 13505-line budget (net 0): the wiring rides on existing lines and one four-line comment was folded to three.
